episode.subject: two blue ribbon eels sharing a reef opening
episode.title: I thought of an answer
episode.body:
I came out to tell him I wasn't speaking to him.

He was already at the opening. I pushed past his chin and began.

He asked whether this counted as speaking.

I went back in.

It was dark in there, and I had thought of an answer.

He hadn't moved. I came up under his chin again.

proposals.visibleScene: Two blue and yellow ribbon eels emerge from the same reef opening. Upper head extends right over the lower head, with both mouths open. Sand, reef roof and skin details sharp.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Rue is the lower eel; this casting and neighbor identity are fictional. Speech, grievance, sequence of emerging, withdrawing and returning are authored fiction. Mouth opening does not prove talking or aggression. Nostril flaps are not ears or hands.
proposals.continuity: Append after existing He recognized the mouth, leaving all ten existing passages and their media decisions untouched. Rue remains blue adult male near Dauin with existing avatar. Beqa Island Fiji is source provenance for compatible Indo-Pacific taxon and habitat, not a narrated journey. Existing Much better for the current invites a withdrawn companion back through an excuse; this Story concerns Rue repeatedly returning to a dispute despite announcing silence.
proposals.biologyEvidence: Australian Museum full species account independently opened: blue/yellow adult male appearance, expanded anterior nostrils, sand/rubble burrows beside coral reefs and Indo-west Pacific range.
proposals.review: Image pass and prose pass by author. Root independently opened image and provisionally found draft distinct before final metadata package. Preserve embedded credit.

episode.subject: two blue-legged hermit crabs close together on reef
episode.title: Nothing on the shell
episode.body:
He said something kept catching the back of his shell.

I went round to look. Nothing there.

He walked a few steps. Stopped. Said it had happened again.

I checked once more, then stayed where I was while he moved.

This time he kept going.

After that I followed with my claws to myself.

proposals.visibleScene: Large foreground blue-legged hermit crab faces viewer, with both spotted claws and patterned eyes legible. Another crab appears immediately behind on the right, with a second eye and blue legs. Exact shell-to-claw contact is not resolved.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Clove narrates as the rear crab. Inspection, movement, complaints and his own repeated touching are fiction around this crowded pair. No witnessed behavioral sequence is claimed. Neither animal molts, changes shell, or has a demonstrated age/sex assigned from photo.
proposals.continuity: Append after existing Room to disappear. Preserve all eleven original episodes and old/new shell sequence. No new shell change or relative age assertion. Key Largo remains home; West Bay Cayman Islands is compatible western Atlantic image provenance, not a narrated relocation.
proposals.biologyEvidence: Primary research abstract identifies Clibanarius tricolor as a western Atlantic shell-using marine hermit crab. The study concerns population and reproduction, not proof of the authored shell inspection or cooperation.
proposals.review: Prose has a distinct consequence: repeated helpful inspection delays recognition of his own intrusive claw, then he changes how he follows. Author proposes for lead judgment but marks image dependency: both crabs are visible, contact is not. Hold if the specific physical gag requires more contact evidence. Unlike occupied-shell and shell-fit passages, no acquisition, eviction, handling or retreat into a shell occurs.
